$comment: Relay 2.0 per-model probe orchestration (per-model protocol probing). Candidate order only decides which protocol a 1-token probe tries first; it is never a source, never stored, never shown as a badge. A passing probe stores `reachable` on that model only and its root in relayRequested.resolvedAPIBaseURLs[transport]; the connection default protocol is never changed by probing. Short protocol names map to wire values through `transports`. new-api `supported_endpoint_types` cases come from gateway-models.v1.json (records + expected.candidates); this file holds the family path, the by-model lookup and the orchestration scenarios. Each end runs every case and scenario under the same caseId inside tests named after the RL2-PROBE-0N id.

candidateRules.$comment: 1) Map the model's supported_endpoint_types in array order through endpointTypeToCandidate, drop unknown values and duplicates; if anything survives, that is the order. 2) Otherwise look the model up in the Server by-model view (GET /api/metadata/model-facts?view=by-model): key = normalizeModelFactsID(id) (same as Server normalizeModelsDevJoinID); on a miss, retry with the segment after the last '/' of that normalized id (same as Server modelsDevJoinLastSegment fallback). A hit's family selects familyCandidates; a miss, an unknown family, or a failed / unavailable view selects defaultCandidates. Never guess a family from the model id text. 3) Keep at most maxCandidates.
candidateRules.explicitConnection: When the connection transport is not 'auto' (the user chose it, or the address carries a protocol path), a model without its own protocol follows the connection and is never probed: enabling it and redetect send no probe request and write no model field, and the send-time protocol fallback has no other candidate. supported_endpoint_types, the family lookup and a discovered generation route are ignored for that connection. The add flow still verifies the sample model with one request on the connection protocol.

probeOutcomeRules.$comment: What one probe request means. pass -> store reachable on that protocol and stop. routeRejected -> this protocol path does not serve this model; try the next candidate. inconclusive -> nothing was learned (bad key, rate limit, upstream trouble, a parameter the gateway disliked): stop at once, send no further candidate with the same key, write no model field. routeRejected is exactly the send-time protocol fallback trigger (negative-cache.v1.json protocolFallbackRules); the two must share one predicate on each end. http_403_route is a 403 whose body contains one of protocolFallbackRules.phrases; any other 403 is http_403. html_200 is a 2xx whose body is a web page (the gateway's SPA fallback, i.e. the path is not an API route; same recognition as RelaySuccessResponsePolicy ).

probeRequestRules.$comment: A probe is the chat request with a one-message conversation. It is built by the same request builder as a chat send on that protocol (same headers, same identity / storage / cache fields), so a gateway that validates the client sees one shape. Only the conversation, streaming and the output cap differ. responsesMaxOutputTokens is the official lower bound of the Responses API; the other protocols keep 1.

byModelResponse.$comment: Shape of the Server by-model view body. Fake servers in tests serve exactly this.

generationRouteCases.$comment: When the add flow found no catalog and discovery only reached a generation route (detection evidence generation_probe) with protocol `route`, that protocol is the first candidate for the first selected model; the candidateRules result for the model follows, duplicates dropped, at most maxCandidates. Test ids RD2-ROUTE-<caseId>; byModelResponse is the by-model view used for the family lookup.

scenarios.$comment: connection = relay connection before the step (transport 'auto' means the user did not choose one). models[].supportedEndpointTypes is what the catalog returned for that id. ping maps '<modelId>@<short transport>' to one of the outcomes in probeOutcomeRules; anything unlisted is http_404. Only ok passes; only a routeRejected outcome moves on to the next candidate, an inconclusive one ends the step . expect.pings is the exact ordered list of probe requests the step sends; expect.models lists the Relay 2.0 fields per model after the step (absent key = nil); expect.connectionTransport is relayRequested.transport after the step. expect.resolvedAPIBaseURLs is exactly the set of entries the probe step itself writes; a root recorded by connection-level catalog discovery (which depends on each end's catalog discovery order) is outside these scenarios and asserted by the end's own discovery tests.

A Relay model whose id matches the official Anthropic catalog entry that carries nativeFileMimes / pdfNativeDefault (reuse the end's S0 test catalog). With relayTransport anthropic_messages: source reachable -> nativeFileMimes empty and pdfNativeDefault false; source observed or user -> both inherited exactly as S0 does today.

Only a model whose relayTransport is set with source reachable, and whose relayTransport at completion equals the protocol the send started with, becomes observed. A model following the connection (nil) stays nil; user stays user; a failed or partial send changes nothing.

Before the step every listed model is enabled and the connection has entries in the end's existing per-connection negative caches (capability rejection cache and tool-call memory). After: reachable is cleared on every model, then every enabled model whose relayTransport is nil after clearing is re-probed, in enabled order (relay connections have no default model; the defaultModel field below is legacy isDefault data and must be ignored); observed / user / tested overrides stay; no enabled model is removed; both negative caches hold nothing for this connection; the connection protocol is unchanged.
Run once per outcome in probeOutcomeRules.inconclusive in place of http_429: the second candidate would pass, yet it is never sent.
